Why this exists

Chat is good for instructions. Work needs a place.

Augmentor can reason in the session and work in the repository. The workbench adds a shared surface for results that are visual, interactive, or decision-heavy.

See the result

Presentations, prototypes, dashboards, decision gates, and Craft views appear directly in the browser.

Act on the result

The human can navigate, choose, approve, or respond without translating the artifact back into chat.

Keep the project real

The HTML remains a project file. The workbench displays durable revisions instead of becoming a second source of truth.

The integration

Augmentor becomes the first workbench client

The workbench stays agent-agnostic. Augmentor is the first adapter that turns a ResonantOS session into published HTML and receives the human response.

ResonantOS User starts the task
→
Augmentor Reasons, builds, publishes
→
Workbench Stores and serves the revision
→
Human Inspects and responds
The response travels back as an event, so Augmentor can continue the same task with the human's decision.

One continuous task

From request to interaction

Ask

“Create a presentation for our ResonantOS call.”

Build

Augmentor creates or updates an HTML file inside the project.

Publish

The file becomes a committed workbench revision.

Interact

The human reviews the result and makes a choice in context.

Continue

Augmentor receives the event and resumes with new evidence.

Proof boundary

What this demo proves, and what comes next

Working now

  • A local server hosts the workbench.
  • An agent session can publish complete project HTML.
  • The canvas loads the committed revision.
  • The artifact remains interactive and navigable.

Next integration slice

  • Launch or connect it from ResonantOS.
  • Bind an Augmentor session to a canvas surface.
  • Add append, replace, refresh, and scoped region operations.
  • Return typed user events with approval receipts.

The first useful version

Augmentor does the work. The workbench makes it tangible.

Start with one honest loop: create project HTML, publish it, let the human interact, and return that response to the session.

Phase 01

Publish

Complete HTML from an Augmentor task appears in the local canvas.

Phase 02

Respond

Typed interactions travel from the canvas back to the active session.

Phase 03

Compose

Scoped operations let the agent evolve parts of the page without rebuilding everything.
